title: Characterise out-of-range (r, s) acceptance in acme-sign 1.4.2
researchQuestion: Which out-of-range (r, s) pairs does acme-sign 1.4.2 verify() accept, and is the acceptance confined to r = 0?
motivation: Run #3 accepted one fixed case (r = 0, s = 0) and run #4 accepted two zero-component vectors. Eight fixed cases cannot say whether the defect is confined to zero components or whether other out-of-range values are accepted.

sourceReferences.label: Standard ECDSA verification requires 1 <= r, s <= n-1 (sample reference, no citation)

hypothesis: H1: acceptance is confined to pairs with r = 0; every sampled pair with r in [1, n-1] or r >= n is rejected.
baselineAndControls: Control: the same 2000 pairs are presented to the reference verifier, which must accept none. Baseline: run #3 (7 of 8 fixed cases rejected).
procedure: Sample 2000 pairs from a seeded generator mixing r or s in {0, n, n+1, 2n, 2^256-1} with random in-range partners; verify each against message m1 with key 1 (seed 7001); record accept/reject per case; run the control; write an evidence record.

outcomes.success: H1 holds: all accepted pairs have r = 0 and the control accepts none.
outcomes.failure: H1 refuted: pairs with r != 0 are accepted, or the control accepts any pair.
outcomes.inconclusive: The run does not finish within 120 s, or repeats with the same seed disagree.

safetyBoundaries: Synthetic keys and messages only; sandbox with networking disabled; allowlisted signature fixture only; no production material.
wouldEstablish: Which classes of out-of-range input this version accepts, under this sample.
wouldNotEstablish: Exploitability in Acme's deployment, correctness of the signing path, or behaviour outside the sampled classes.

protocolHistory.note: Approved as protocol v1. Synthetic keys only; record the generator seed.

resultSummary: Run #10 (1.4.2): 63 of 2000 pairs accepted, all with r = 0; control accepted none. H1 holds for this sample. Run #14 (1.4.3, same seed): 0 of 2000 accepted.
followUpSuggestions: Exhaustive check of the small set {0, 1, n-1, n, n+1} x {0, 1, n-1, n, n+1} to complement the sample.
Verify that the signing path never produces r = 0 or s = 0 (RFC 6979-style regeneration), as a separate experiment.
Repeat the sweep with a second seed to check sampling sensitivity.

title: Separate library latency from measurement setup effects
researchQuestion: Is the p99 difference between run #5 (2.60 ms) and run #6 (1.62 ms) explained by the missing warm-up, or does 1.4.2 have a genuine tail-latency problem?
motivation: Two agents disagree about run #5. Agreement between agents would not settle it; a repeated measurement with and without warm-up can.
hypothesis: H1: with warm-up, five repeats across sandbox slots all report p99 within 2.0 ms; without warm-up, p99 exceeds 2.0 ms in at least four of five repeats.
baselineAndControls: Control: the reference verifier measured under the same two regimes. Baseline: runs #5 and #6.
procedure: For each regime (warm-up 0, warm-up 200), run the latency test five times on different sandbox slots; record p50/p95/p99 per repeat; compare distributions.

outcomes.success: H1 holds: the warm-up regime explains the difference.
outcomes.failure: Warm-up runs also exceed 2.0 ms in some repeats: a genuine tail-latency issue exists on this profile.
outcomes.inconclusive: Repeats disagree without a pattern, or fewer than four repeats complete per regime.

safetyBoundaries: Synthetic keys only; sandbox with networking disabled.
wouldEstablish: Whether the run #5 figure reflects the library or the measurement setup, on the reference profile.
